arxiv-2207-13418.title: Bayesian Dynamic Network Modelling: an application to metabolic associations in cardiovascular diseases
arxiv-2207-13418.creator: Marco Molinari, Andrea Cremaschi, Maria De Iorio, Nishi Chaturvedi, Alun Hughes, Therese Tillin
arxiv-2207-13418.description: Abstract Abstract : We propose a novel approach to the estimation of multiple Graphical Models to analyse temporal patterns of association among a set of metabolites over different groups of patients. Our motivating application is the Southall And Brent REvisited (SABRE) study, a tri-ethnic cohort study conducted in the UK.

arxiv-2301-03588.title: Multiscale Metamorphic VAE for 3D Brain MRI Synthesis
arxiv-2301-03588.creator: Jaivardhan Kapoor, Jakob H. Macke, Christian F. Baumgartner
arxiv-2301-03588.description: Abstract Generative modeling of 3D brain MRIs presents difficulties in achieving high visual fidelity while ensuring sufficient coverage of the data distribution. In this work, we propose to address this challenge with composable, multiscale morphological transformations in a variational autoencoder (VAE) framework.

arxiv-2303-11400.title: Correlation constraints and the Bloch geometry of two qubits
arxiv-2303-11400.creator: Simon Morelli, Christopher Eltschka, Marcus Huber, Jens Siewert
arxiv-2303-11400.description: Abstract We present a novel inequality on the purity of a bipartite state depending solely on the length-difference of the local Bloch vectors. For two qubits this inequality is tight for all marginal states and so extends the previously known solution for the 2-qubit marginal problem.

arxiv-2311-07792.title: Western, Religious or Spiritual: An Evaluation of Moral Justification in Large Language Models
arxiv-2311-07792.creator: Eyup Engin Kucuk, Muhammed Yusuf Kocyigit
arxiv-2311-07792.description: Abstract The increasing success of Large Language Models (LLMs) in variety of tasks lead to their widespread use in our lives which necessitates the examination of these models from different perspectives. The alignment of these models to human values is an essential concern in order to establish trust that we have safe and responsible systems.

arxiv-2405-06913.title: Tachibana operator Applied to Invariant submanifolds of Lorentzian trans-Sasakian manifolds
arxiv-2405-06913.creator: Mehmet Atc̣eken and Tugba Mert
arxiv-2405-06913.description: Abstract . In the present paper, Tachibana operatory is applied to an invariant submanifold of a lorentzian trans-Sasakian manifold by means of through various tensors and the results obtained are discussed in terms of geometry. Finally, we give a non-trivial example in order to our results illustrate. 1991 Mathematics Subject Classification 53C15; 53C42 1.

arxiv-2410-01767.title: Utility-Directed Conformal Prediction: A Decision-Aware Framework for Actionable Uncertainty Quantification
arxiv-2410-01767.creator: Santiago Cortes-Gomez, Carlos Patiño *, Yewon Byun, Zhiwei Steven Wu, Eric Horvitz † & Bryan Wilder
arxiv-2410-01767.description: Abstract Interest has been growing in decision-focused machine learning methods which train models to account for how their predictions are used in downstream optimization problems. Doing so can often improve performance on subsequent decision problems. However, current methods for uncertainty quantification do not incorporate any information about downstream decisions.

arxiv-2505-14951.title: MultiMAE Meets Earth Observation: Pre-training Multi-modal Multi-task Masked Autoencoders for Earth Observation Tasks
arxiv-2505-14951.creator: Jose Sosa, Danila Rukhovich, Anis Kacem, Djamila Aouada
arxiv-2505-14951.description: Abstract Multi-modal data in Earth Observation (EO) presents a huge opportunity for improving transfer learning capabilities when pre-training deep learning models. Unlike prior work that often overlooks multi-modal EO data, recent methods have started to include it, resulting in more effective pre-training strategies.

pmc-10575117.title: Effect of Eco-Friendly Application of Bee Honey Solution on Yield, Physio-Chemical, Antioxidants, and Enzyme Gene Expressions in Excessive Nitrogen-Stressed Common Bean (Phaseolus vulgaris L.) Plants
pmc-10575117.creator: Hussein E E Belal, Mostafa A M Abdelpary, El-Sayed M Desoky, Esmat F Ali, Najla Amin T Al Kashgry, Mostafa M Rady, Wael M Semida, Amr E M Mahmoud, Ali A S Sayed, Arafat Abdel Hamed Abdel Latef, Narendra Singh Yadav
pmc-10575117.description: Excessive use of nitrogen (N) pollutes the environment and causes greenhouse gas emissions; however, the application of eco-friendly plant biostimulators (BSs) can overcome these issues. Therefore, this paper aimed to explore the role of diluted bee honey solution (DHS) in attenuating the adverse impacts of N toxicity on Phaseolus vulgaris growth, yield quality, physio-chemical properties, and defense systems.

pmc-10747855.title: Universal Approach to Integrating Reduced Graphene Oxide into Polymer Electronics
pmc-10747855.creator: Elena Abyzova, Ilya Petrov, Ilya Bril’, Dmitry Cheshev, Alexey Ivanov, Maxim Khomenko, Andrey Averkiev, Maxim Fatkullin, Dmitry Kogolev, Evgeniy Bolbasov, Aleksandar Matkovic, Jin-Ju Chen, Raul D Rodriguez, Evgeniya Sheremet, Naveen Tiwari
pmc-10747855.description: Flexible electronics have sparked significant interest in the development of electrically conductive polymer-based composite materials. While efforts are being made to fabricate these composites through laser integration techniques, a versatile methodology applicable to a broad range of thermoplastic polymers remains elusive. Moreover, the underlying mechanisms driving the formation of such composites are not thoroughly understood.

pmc-12557160.title: Yoga-based cardiac rehabilitation in the Hospital of Cittadella (Province of Padua), Italy
pmc-12557160.creator: A Ruffatto, N Cogo, F Saladini, G Povolo, C Scarabello, R C Napolitano, M Serafini, S Bevilacqua, A Madia, E Zilli
pmc-12557160.description: IssueCardiovascular diseases are the most common cause of mortality in Western countries. Cardiac rehabilitation aims to reduce recurrence and mortality, as well as improving the quality of life in patients who have undergone Acute Myocardial Infarction and Cardiovascular diseases. Lifestyle modification plays a crucial role in secondary prevention.

pmc-12692724.title: Sex and Ethnic Disparities in Stroke Revascularisation Treatments and Post-Stroke Outcomes in Patients with Heart Failure: A National Inpatient Sample Study
pmc-12692724.creator: Ali L Al-Batat, Tiberiu A Pana, Mamas A Mamas, Evangelos Kontopantelis, Phyo K Myint, Rudiger J Seitz, Daniele Piovani
pmc-12692724.description: Background/Objectives: We aimed to determine sex and racial/ethnic disparities in associations between Acute Ischaemic stroke (AIS) with co-morbid heart failure (HF) and in-hospital outcomes, using the US National Inpatient Sample (NIS) in this retrospective observational study based on administrative data. Methods: AIS admissions from January 2016 to December 2019 were extracted from the NIS.

pmc-13369311.title: Artificial-Intelligence-Driven Electromyography Adaptation for Elderly Assistance at Physiological, Functional, and Behavioral Levels
pmc-13369311.creator: Jiaqi Xue, Ziqi Li, Xiaoyang Zou, Zijia Qu, Shengjie Yang, Colin Pak Yu Chan, Yanchen Liu, Zhou Zhao, Jing Zhang, Clio Yuen Man Cheng, Haiyang Wang, Kehan Zou, Yafei Zhao, Vivian Weiqun Lou, Ning Xi, King Wai Chiu Lai
pmc-13369311.description: Older adults frequently face difficulties in activities of daily living (ADLs) due to age-related declines in strength, coordination, and perception. Myoelectric control provides an intuitive human–robot interface by translating muscle activity into assistive commands. However, its practical application is still challenged by signal annotation, multijoint coordination, and cross-task generalization.
